facts.heading: Exhausted since October
facts.content: Daniel has been completely burned out since October. He feels exhausted and is running on fumes.
facts.evidence: I've been completely burned out since October.

facts.heading: Work situation caused burnout
facts.content: Daniel lost a big client, and half the team moved onto a rescue plan. He ended up doing three people's jobs.
facts.evidence: We lost a big client, and half the team got moved onto the rescue plan, so I ended up doing three people's jobs.

facts.heading: Work bleeds into personal time
facts.content: Daniel is still answering work messages at ten at night and thinks about work even when not working.
facts.evidence: I'm at my desk by seven and I'm still answering messages at ten at night. Even when I'm not working I'm thinking about work.

facts.heading: Poor sleep quality
facts.content: Daniel's sleep is terrible, and he sleeps about four hours most nights.
facts.evidence: Most nights I sleep about four hours.

facts.heading: Wakes up at three AM
facts.content: Daniel wakes up at three in the morning and cannot fall back asleep.
facts.evidence: I wake up at three in the morning and can't fall back asleep.

facts.heading: Thoughts during wakefulness
facts.content: When Daniel wakes up, he thinks about shipping schedules, the client, or if he forgot something.
facts.evidence: My head just starts. Shipping schedules, the client, whether I've forgotten something.

facts.heading: Dreading the nights
facts.content: Daniel has started dreading the nights.
facts.evidence: I've started dreading the nights, if I'm honest.

facts.heading: Father diagnosed with Parkinson's
facts.content: Daniel's father was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.
facts.evidence: My father. He was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.

facts.heading: Father's current condition
facts.content: Daniel's father's hands shake, he is slower, and he gets frustrated.
facts.evidence: His hands shake, and he's slower, and he gets frustrated.

facts.heading: Daniel drives father to hospital
facts.content: Daniel drives his father to the hospital in Leeds for neurology appointments every few weeks.
facts.evidence: I'm the one who drives him to the hospital in Leeds. The neurology appointments are every few weeks, and it's an hour each way.

facts.heading: Younger sister lives in Toronto
facts.content: Daniel's younger sister Hannah lives in Toronto, and all care for their father falls on Daniel.
facts.evidence: My younger sister Hannah lives in Toronto, so all the care for our father falls on me.

facts.heading: Daniel feels guilty about care
facts.content: Daniel feels guilty for saying it, feeling selfish to be tired when his father is ill.
facts.evidence: Guilty for even saying it. I feel it's selfish to be tired when he's the one who's ill.

facts.heading: Daniel hides his exhaustion
facts.content: Daniel does not tell Hannah about his exhaustion because he feels it is selfish.
facts.evidence: So I don't say anything to anyone.

facts.heading: GP visit results
facts.content: Daniel had blood tests that were all normal. The GP suggested stress and exhaustion.
facts.evidence: She did blood tests, and they were all normal. She said it's stress and exhaustion

facts.heading: Refused to talk to GP
facts.content: Daniel told his GP he had no time to talk about his stress and exhaustion.
facts.evidence: I said I hadn't got time

facts.heading: Girlfriend booked therapy
facts.content: Daniel's girlfriend Claire booked something for him. She said she was done watching him disappear.
facts.evidence: My girlfriend booked it, to be honest. Claire. She said she was done watching me disappear.

facts.heading: Claire is patient
facts.content: Claire is patient and makes Daniel tea without pushing him to talk.
facts.evidence: She's very patient. She makes me tea and doesn't push me to talk.

facts.heading: Claire is worn out
facts.content: Daniel sees that Claire is also wearing out.
facts.evidence: But I can see it's wearing on her too.

facts.heading: Claire stopped weekend plans
facts.content: Claire stopped asking Daniel to go away for the weekend. Daniel always says no.
facts.evidence: She stopped asking if I want to go away for the weekend, because I always say no.

facts.heading: Work emails cause stress
facts.content: Daniel receives two hundred emails if he is away. He worries Dad might need something.
facts.evidence: If I'm away I'll come back to two hundred of them. And Dad might need something.

facts.heading: Cannot take time off
facts.content: Daniel cannot remember the last time he was properly off.
facts.evidence: I can't remember the last time I was properly off.

facts.heading: Stopped running two months ago
facts.content: Daniel stopped running ten kilometres every Saturday morning about two months ago.
facts.evidence: I stopped about two months ago. I ran. Ten kilometres every Saturday morning.

facts.heading: Lost part of self
facts.content: Daniel feels like he has lost a part of himself after stopping running.
facts.evidence: Like I've lost a part of myself.

facts.heading: Running was solitary time
facts.content: Running was the one time in the week nobody could reach Daniel.
facts.evidence: It was the one time in the week nobody could reach me.

facts.heading: Lost motivation to run
facts.content: Daniel stopped running because his legs felt like lead.
facts.evidence: My legs felt like lead, and then I just never went back.

facts.heading: Boss sends late emails
facts.content: Peterson sends emails at eleven at night and expects an answer before breakfast.
facts.evidence: He sends emails at eleven at night and expects an answer before breakfast.

facts.heading: Answers emails constantly
facts.content: Daniel answers every email, even when he is in bed. Claire hates this.
facts.evidence: I answer it. Every time. Even if I'm in bed. Claire hates it.

facts.heading: Fear of job loss
facts.content: Daniel is afraid his boss will think he is not committed due to a restructuring.
facts.evidence: That he'd think I wasn't committed. There's a restructuring in the spring and I'm afraid they'll let me go.

facts.heading: Ambivalent feelings about job loss
facts.content: Daniel thinks he might feel relieved but also horrible about being relieved if he loses his job.
facts.evidence: I think part of me would be relieved, and then I'd feel horrible about being relieved.

facts.heading: Mood is flat and irritable
facts.content: Daniel's moods apart from tiredness are flat and irritable.
facts.evidence: Flat, mostly. And irritable.

facts.heading: Snapping at colleague
facts.content: Daniel snapped at a colleague last week over nothing and sat in the toilets for ten minutes.
facts.evidence: I snapped at a colleague last week over nothing and went and sat in the toilets for ten minutes.

facts.heading: Physical symptoms during anger
facts.content: Daniel's heart was going and his hands were shaking when he snapped at a colleague.
facts.evidence: My heart was going and my hands were shaking.

facts.heading: Fear of heart attack
facts.content: Daniel briefly thought he might have a heart attack when he snapped at a colleague.
facts.evidence: I thought for a second it was a heart attack, but it passed.

facts.heading: Frightening event on train
facts.content: Daniel has experienced a frightening event on a train to Manchester. He had to get off and stand on the platform.
facts.evidence: Once on the train to Manchester. I just had to get off and stand on the platform.

facts.heading: Fear of losing control
facts.content: Daniel is afraid that he is losing it or not coping. He worries about his future state.
facts.evidence: That I'm losing it. That I'm going to end up like, I don't know. Not coping.

facts.heading: Coffee consumption habit
facts.content: Daniel drinks about six cups of coffee a day.
facts.evidence: I'm on about six cups a day.

facts.heading: Evening wine consumption
facts.content: Daniel has started having wine in the evenings to switch his head off. He drinks two to three glasses.
facts.evidence: And I've started having wine in the evenings to switch my head off. Two glasses, sometimes three.

facts.heading: Wine effect on sleep
facts.content: Daniel finds the wine uneasy and notes it does not help him sleep.
facts.evidence: Uneasy. It works for an hour and then I wake at three anyway. I know it's not helping.

facts.heading: Feeling of listing problems
facts.content: Daniel feels that the wine makes him list everything wrong with himself.
facts.evidence: It feels like I'm just listing everything that's wrong with me.

facts.heading: Relief from speaking out
facts.content: Daniel felt a sense of relief after speaking about his feelings today.
facts.evidence: Strange. A bit of a relief, actually. Like putting down a bag I didn't realise I was carrying.

facts.heading: Desire to sleep
facts.content: Daniel thinks that if he could sleep, he could probably cope with the rest.
facts.evidence: The nights, I think. If I could sleep I could probably cope with the rest.

facts.heading: Family influence on coping
facts.content: Daniel's grandfather and father never complained about anything. Daniel feels he should not be weak.
facts.evidence: My grandfather worked in the mines in Yorkshire. He never complained about anything, not once. Dad's the same. You just get on with it.

facts.heading: Belief about being weak
facts.content: Daniel thinks his grandfather would think he was weak for being there.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking he would think I was weak for being here.

facts.heading: Statement about self-worth
facts.content: Daniel stated that he is not weak but very tired. He is unsure if he believes this yet.
facts.evidence: That I'm not weak. I'm just very tired. Maybe. I don't know if I believe it yet.

facts.heading: Proposed coping strategy
facts.content: The therapist suggested a small change: a fixed time to switch off his phone.
facts.evidence: Very small. A fixed time in the evening when you switch off your phone, even for twenty minutes.

facts.heading: Agreed to try strategy
facts.content: Daniel agreed to try the proposed strategy. He suggested half past nine for tea with Claire.
facts.evidence: Yes. Half past nine, perhaps. I could make it a thing with Claire. Tea on the sofa.

facts.heading: Agreed to meet next week
facts.content: Daniel agreed to meet again next week.
facts.evidence: Same time next week? Yes. I'll be here.
